content: Folic acid is prescribed to treat or prevent folic acid deficiency. It is a B-complex vitamin essential for the production of red blood cells in the body. A deficiency in this vitamin can lead to specific types of anemia, characterized by a low red blood cell count. Folic acid is available in tablet form and is typically taken once daily. It is important to follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully. If you have any questions or concerns, consult your doctor or pharmacist for clarification. Take folic acid exactly as directed by your healthcare provider. Do not take more or less of it, or take it more frequently than prescribed. If you are using folic acid to treat a deficiency, you may notice an improvement in your symptoms quickly, often within 24 hours. However, do not discontinue the medication unless instructed to do so by your doctor. This medication may also be prescribed for other purposes. If you have questions about additional uses, consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before taking folic acid, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to folic acid or any other medications. Additionally, provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, especially phenytoin (Dilantin) and any vitamins. Your doctor may recommend increasing your dietary intake of folic acid by consuming more liver, foods made from dried yeast, fruits, and fresh leafy green vegetables. If you forget to take a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Folic acid may cause side effects. If you experience any of the following symptoms, contact your doctor immediately: skin rash, itching, redness, or difficulty breathing. If you experience a severe side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or no longer needed medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on the correct disposal method. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor will order specific lab tests to monitor your response to folic acid. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
